purpose: The bounded first gameplay test of the integrated A/B generated campaigns. The campaign_soak probe (src/MNBL.ProceduralWorld/Automation/CampaignSoakProbe.cs) reads its worlds and rules from this file; tools/summarize_campaign_soak.py checks every scenario below against the run's outputs (with the rules, hours and motion fractions the run recorded) and writes evidence/gameplay/campaign-soak.json. A failure found by a run or the review is added to regressions with what now guards it: a check the in-game run makes, an input the probe validates, or a mutation of the committed fixture (a passing run's trimmed output) that reintroduces the failure and must fail its scenario (tests/Runtime/test_campaign_soak_regressions.py).

scenarios.what: World A's new campaign initializes a coherent state: no invalid reference (owners, bound towns, leaders, rulers, governors, party leaders and clans, armies, home settlements), no settlement, clan or kingdom outside the world or its aliases, every town and castle with a garrison, food and an owner, every town with notables offering volunteers and a market of trade goods (a market sold out later is a recorded state of the economy), every kingdom with a living ruler, every party on valid navigation; lords, lord parties, caravans and bandits present; every semantic route (MMR-41: villages to their bound settlements, starts, capitals, ports) holds in the live campaign (CampaignPlayability: engine paths and the registered navigation caches). Villages without a trade town and towns without gold are recorded.

The player's party travels from its start town to the nearest other town by land (MapDistanceModel, default navigation) that offers it a volunteer and an affordable trade good, and the engine opens that town's settlement encounter (the town menu) on arrival, as when the player clicks the town; the player later leaves through the menu's leave path (PlayerEncounter.LeaveSettlement, Finish). Other parties ignore the player for the whole test (IgnoreByOtherPartiesTill, recorded as setup).

In that town the player buys one trade good and sells it back through the trade screen's logic: an InventoryLogic for the town built as InventoryScreenHelper.OpenScreenAsTrade builds it (the town menu's trade option; a no-op AfterTransfer handler stands in for the screen's refresh), one transfer each way, committed by DoneLogic. The stock moves one item each way, and the player's and the town's gold move by exactly the quoted prices.

In that town the player recruits one volunteer from a notable (the installed recruitment screen's domain sequence, RecruitmentVM.OnDone): the roster gains the troop, the gold drops by the model's cost, the notable's slot empties. The game decides the volunteer on offer, its availability and its cost.

One campaign day of natural simulation with the player sheltered and holding: time advances without stalls, with no exception thrown from campaign code and no engine assert (both hooks proven by canaries); at least half of the lords, caravans, villagers and bandits move; no party leaves valid navigation, none has its path to a settlement not found (MobileParty._aiPathNotFound, read every frame) or stays stuck (travelling by its short-term behaviour yet not moving) for the stuck window, and no villager holds still for it without an installed reason (home village raided, target town besieged or at war; War Sails' fishing parties, a kind of their own, hold while fishing at their fishing point or roaming); caravans trade in towns, villagers sell their village's goods on entering their towns (SellGoodsForTradeAction.ApplyByVillagerTrade), lords recruit, no town runs out of food, no town is without gold for the whole day.

After the day: volunteer slots empty at the start refill through the installed daily update across the world (operability, not a rate); the player's emptied slot and the traded good's town stock are recorded with the model's daily refill chance.

A war declared between two kingdoms at peace, the target holding two or more fiefs (DeclareWarAction.ApplyByDefault): both stances at war and the event raised; the following hours' AI reaction is recorded as natural behaviour.

A town of the war's target passed to a lord of the declarer (ChangeOwnerOfSettlementAction.ApplyByDefault): owner clan, faction, bound villages, both clans' fiefs and the garrison follow, its notables stay, any governor is of the new clan, the event names both owners, and the target, keeping a fief, survives and stays at war (a kingdom left without fiefs is dissolved by the installed FactionDiscontinuationCampaignBehavior, as run 21164 showed).

A clan leader with adult kin dies of old age (KillCharacterAction.ApplyByOldAge), a clan with fiefs preferred: an heir of the clan leads it, the clan keeps its fiefs, the leader-changed event is raised, and nothing refers to the dead hero as a leader, governor or party member.

A kingdom's ruler dies of old age, a kingdom with two or more candidate clans preferred: the outcome is the installed rule's (KillCharacterAction.ApplyInternal) for its candidates (clans not eliminated, not mercenaries, not led by the dead ruler): two or more, a king selection is added and, for a kingdom other than the player's, held at once by Kingdom.AddDecision (KingdomElection.StartElection), applying the elected ruling clan, one of the candidates (a ruling clan without an heir then gives the rule to another eligible clan); one, that clan rules; none, the kingdom is destroyed. The kingdom keeps a living leader of its ruling clan, and nothing refers to the dead ruler.

Six campaign hours after the diagnostic actions: time advances without stalls, campaign exceptions or engine asserts, the state stays coherent (no invalid reference, no party off navigation), and the war (elimination told apart from peace), the new owner and the heirs are recorded as the simulation left them.

World B (MMR-19's fixture world, started after A ended in the same process) initializes its own state: nothing of A is registered or referenced, its campaign time starts fresh, its parties, notables, markets and food are its own and coherent, and its semantic routes hold in the live campaign (its fixture replaces no creation culture's start, so its refused player-start route is recorded as not applicable).
Twelve campaign hours of B: time advances without stalls, campaign exceptions or engine asserts, at least half of its lords and caravans move on valid navigation, the state stays coherent.
No game and every tracked static at its baseline at the start and after each world ends.

regressions.failure: The trade through InventoryLogic moved the goods but settled no gold: a NullReferenceException after the transfer (run 4652), then one in the TransactionDebt setter (run 34968), before DoneLogic.
regressions.cause: InventoryLogic invokes four callbacks unchecked that the inventory screen's view model hooks: the AfterTransfer and AfterReset events and the TotalAmountChange and DonationXpChange actions; the headless logic had none.
regressions.fix: No-op handlers stand in for all four (the screen's refresh); the exception's full text is recorded if a trade fails.

regressions.failure: The nearest other town offered the player no volunteer (its notables' slots within the player's relation limit were empty), so no recruitment happened.
regressions.cause: VolunteerModel.MaximumIndexHeroCanRecruitFromHero limits a stranger to a notable's lowest slots; the probe picked the town by distance alone.
regressions.fix: The visit goes to the nearest town by land that offers the player a volunteer and an affordable trade good; nearer towns skipped are recorded.

regressions.failure: 34 villager parties held still at sea for six hours, counted as holding without an installed reason.
regressions.cause: They are War Sails' fishing parties (NavalDLC.FishingPartyComponent extends VillagerPartyComponent, naval only): FishingPartyCampaignBehavior holds them at their fishing point while IsFishing.
regressions.fix: Fishing parties are a kind of their own; a fishing party's hold is explained while it is fishing or roaming, otherwise it fails like a villager's.

regressions.failure: World B's route check failed one route: 'no town can be a player start'.
regressions.cause: MMR-19's fixture world replaces no creation culture's start point, so MMR-41's player-start route has nothing to hold there.
regressions.fix: With no starts checked the refused player-start route is recorded as not applicable; every other route must hold.

regressions.failure: The player's trade went through SellItemsAction, which only AI parties use: run 47176's check that the town received the price failed by 2 gold (the town keeps the price less a tax and books a security-adjusted commission).
regressions.cause: The probe used the AI trade action; the trade screen commits through InventoryLogic.DoneLogic (the town's MerchantInventoryListener and GiveGoldAction).
regressions.fix: The trade goes through an InventoryLogic built as InventoryScreenHelper.OpenScreenAsTrade builds it, committed by DoneLogic.

regressions.failure: The visit targeted the town the player starts at: 0 distance, 0 travel hours; no pathing was exercised.
regressions.cause: The nearest town to the start position is the start town.
regressions.fix: The visit goes to the nearest other town by land and requires travel time and no encounter before the move.

regressions.failure: Two looter parties holding by choice (short-term Hold) were counted stuck.
regressions.cause: MobileParty.IsMoving is only Position != MoveTargetPoint for an AI party.
regressions.fix: Stuck requires a travelling short-term behaviour (neither Hold nor None); holding parties are recorded with their state, and a villager holding without an installed reason fails.

regressions.cause: MbEvent.AddNonSerializedListener puts a listener at the head of the list and InvokeList walks from the head, so the probe's SettlementEntered listener ran before VillagerCampaignBehavior's sale.
regressions.fix: The goods, trade gold and town gold are taken on entry (before the sale) and compared at the next hour.

regressions.failure: The expectation awaited a pending king selection; none was pending.
regressions.cause: Kingdom.AddDecision holds the election of a kingdom other than the player's at once (KingdomElection.StartElection); with one candidate clan (run 47176) no election is held at all.
regressions.fix: The expectation follows KillCharacterAction.ApplyInternal and Kingdom.AddDecision branch by branch, and a kingdom with two or more candidates is preferred.

regressions.failure: Taking the war target's only town dissolved the kingdom (FactionDiscontinuationCampaignBehavior), voiding the war it was meant to follow; the follow-up read the elimination as peace.
regressions.cause: Seed 42 has 40 kingdoms for 45 towns (MMR-31: one kingdom per realm with a town), most holding a single fief.
regressions.fix: The war target holds two or more fiefs; the ownership row requires it to survive at war, and the follow-up tells elimination from peace.

regressions.failure: Town mnbl_1609fb72_t_30a1119e46 starts world A with 0 gold, so it buys nothing from villagers or caravans until it earns some.
regressions.cause: Towns start at 0 gold and earn their first through the new-game consumption passes (ItemConsumptionBehavior.MakeConsumptionAllTowns), which pay only for market items in categories with a demand budget; this town's opening market earned nothing. It earns 2277 gold over the first day (run 21164).
regressions.fix: Recorded (the installed economy, not a defect): the audit lists towns without gold, villagers' sales record the town's gold on entry, and a town without gold for the whole day fails.

regressions.failure: Town mnbl_1609fb72_t_7c3c7cce5c sold its last trade-good stack 30 hours in, and the audit counted it as an invalid reference, failing A.after.
regressions.cause: The audit treated a market without trade goods as an incoherent state. World-wide the markets halve in the first hours after the new game and then fall about 7% a day while trade-good stacks restock; one town selling out is a local state of the economy.
regressions.fix: Towns without trade goods are recorded in the census (town:noTradeGoods); every town must stock trade goods at initialization (A.init, B.init).

regressions.failure: World B failed to start after world A's nine minutes: its fixture placement and catalog receipt paths were empty.
regressions.cause: The probe read B's inputs only when it reached B.
regressions.fix: The scenario file names B's inputs; the probe checks every input and file before any game starts, and the offline check validates the fields.

guard.check: CampaignSoakProbe.Body validates every scenario input before world A; check_campaign_soak_scenarios.py validates each world's fields
